title: Free Market Capitalism vs State Intervention
rootClaim: Unregulated free market capitalism produces superior economic growth, human innovation, and resource allocation compared to state-managed economies.

branches.text: Hayekian Knowledge Problem: Centralized state planners cannot synthesize decentralized, real-time market price signals required for efficient resource distribution.

children.text: Market price mechanisms aggregate consumer preferences and supply scarcity across millions of actors without requiring bureaucratic oversight.
Algorithmic Big Data & AI Planning: High-performance compute and neural supply chain forecasting can theoretically calculate equilibrium prices without free market chaotic volatility.
Tacit Knowledge Incommunicability: Human economic choices rely on qualitative, unquantifiable personal context that cannot be codified into algorithms.
Private ownership and profit incentives drive disruptive innovation, technological breakthrough, and capital efficiency.

branches.text: Unchecked free markets produce severe market failures, extreme wealth inequality, and catastrophic environmental degradation.

children.text: Negative Externalities: Industrial pollution and carbon emissions impose unpriced costs onto society when carbon is not state-regulated or taxed.
Coase Theorem: If property rights are well-defined and transaction costs are low, private actors will bargain to internalize externalities without state intervention.
High Transaction Cost Reality: Global environmental damage involves billions of affected parties, rendering private bargaining impossible.
Natural Monopoly & Capital Accumulation: Free competition naturally tends toward monopolistic consolidation and dynastic wealth concentration, suppressing free competition.
Schumpeterian Creative Destruction: Market monopolies are inherently temporary because disruptive startup innovation continually undermines dominant legacy firms.
Keynesian Demand Failure: Unregulated markets suffer from systemic liquidity traps and recessionary spirals that necessitate counter-cyclical state fiscal intervention.

definitions.description: F.A. Hayek's observation that essential economic data is dispersed across millions of individuals as tacit knowledge and cannot be centralized.
Economic proposition that under zero transaction costs, private bargaining will lead to an efficient outcome regardless of initial property right allocation.
Joseph Schumpeter's concept of economic process where radical innovations incessantly revolutionize economic structures by destroying old firms.
A cost imposed on a third party as a consequence of an economic transaction between others (e.g., industrial pollution).
A situation where monetary policy becomes ineffective because interest rates are near zero and individuals hoard cash rather than investing.
